brief_text:

Status: complete

Timeline: Model forecast assumes Invitation for Bids notice type, 28-day advertising period, 7862-character notice length, and English language; peer group benchmark is from Turkey Request for Bids civil works contracts. [forecast:5fdadbe55163, benchmark:country_method_category-d495d284]
  model forecast for this package: median 135 days from tender notice to signing (P10 76, P90 289); probability of a slow tender 30% [forecast:5fdadbe55163]
  peer group: median 132 days; 90th percentile 272 days [benchmark:country_method_category-d495d284]
  the forecast median is 3 days longer than the peer-group median

Market approach: Use Request for Bids method as all five close precedents from the same region used this method, with firms in award notices ranging from 3 to 13, and the country-method-category benchmark shows 25 contracts in this peer group. [contract:1710851, contract:1710611, contract:1711394, contract:1816777, contract:1813924, benchmark:country_method_category-d495d284]

  1. Payment delays to contractors can affect implementation progress. -> Reinforce coordination within implementing departments to reduce invoice processing times and avoid retaining contract guarantees until all works are tested. [lesson_chunk:P145529-34182967-0074]
  2. Design finalization delays can postpone procurement commencement. -> Finalize designs, drawings, and bid documents early in the project cycle to enable on-time contract awards. [lesson_chunk:P123828-34118211-0065]
  3. Low competition may require rebidding of contracts. -> Frame reasonable competitive qualification criteria in bid documents to attract competition during the bidding process. [lesson_chunk:P123828-34118211-0065, lesson_chunk:P124639-33763091-0070]
  4. Contractor performance delays can extend contract completion times. -> Introduce clauses requiring minimum physical progress rates with penalties for underperformance and bonuses for overperformance. [lesson_chunk:P151832-33952864-0065]
